question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 13 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 29 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 10 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity = LCM(13, 29, 10) = 3770 units

Combined Efficiency = (3770 ÷ 13) + (3770 ÷ 29) + (3770 ÷ 10) = 290 + 130 + 377 = 797 units/hour

Time required together = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency = 3770 ÷ 797

On converting to a mixed fraction, Time = 4 ⁵⁸²/₇₉₇ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 ⁵⁸²/₇₉₇ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A = 13 hours

Time taken by pipe B = 29 hours

Time taken by pipe C = 10 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of times taken by individual pipes

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Time = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of A, B and C = 290 + 130 + 377 = 797 units/hour

⇒ Time taken when all pipes operate together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time = 3770 ÷ 797

⇒ Time = 4 ⁵⁸²/₇₉₇ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 ⁵⁸²/₇₉₇ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills a tank, hence its efficiency is taken as positive. An outlet pipe or a leak empties the tank, so its efficiency is taken as negative.

Work Equivalence Rule

If M₁ workers do W₁ work in D₁ days working H₁ hours/day, and M₂ workers do W₂ work in D₂ days working H₂ hours/day, then (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Alternate Hours Concept

If pipes operate on alternate hours, calculate the combined work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 3 hours if 3 pipes alternate) and then find the maximum number of full cycles possible before calculating the remaining fractional part.
